title: POC weekly sync - quality evaluation & regression check
summary: Weekly POC sync to review latest quality evals (prompt sets and scoring), investigate a small regression on discharge-summary QA, discuss guardrails and alerting, and align next steps for expanded evals and security docs.
topics: Security docs request and next demo
action_items: Avery - share detailed scoring spreadsheet and per-prompt failure cases by 2025-10-17
Marco - run 50k evaluation with int8 quantized model and attach latency distribution by 2025-10-21
Priya - provide 200 new prompt examples covering edge-case diagnoses by 2025-10-20
Tom - confirm infra constraint (VPC egress rules) and send network contact by 2025-10-16
next_steps: Redwood to run expanded eval with new prompts and return updated pass/fail heatmap
Customer to prioritize top 3 workflows for canary rollout
Schedule technical deep-dive for private deployment options (if latency improvement needed)
Redwood to share security pack and SOC2 summary for procurement
transcript: [00:00] Avery Chen (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:05] Priya Nair (Nexigen): Priya here, ML lead. good to be back.
[00:07] Tom Blake (Nexigen): Tom, engineering manager. Sara and Jordan are on as well.
[00:12] Marco Ruiz (Redwood): Marco from SE, I'll take the evaluation deck run-through.
[00:20] Avery: Alright, agenda — quick results summary, deep dive on the discharge-summary regression, prompt set changes, and then next steps. Marco, you wanna start?

[00:28] Marco: Sure. so this week we ran the v3 prompt set across the 10k eval harness — sorry, 10k, yes — and overall pass rate for the three core tasks is roughly 86% up from 83 last week. but there's a localized drop on the discharge-summary QA: pass rate down to 74 from 85, odd spike.
[00:49] Priya: Wait, 74? that's a pretty big shift. did you change temperature or model variant?

[00:55] Marco: No we kept generation params the same: temp 0.0, top_p 0.95 for nucleus sampling on the classification head. the major change was prompt_wrapping in v3 to include more context tokens and a prefix filter to reduce hallucination. We suspect the longer context triggers kv-cache truncation effect on the quantized variant.
[01:15] Tom: Can you unpack kv-cache truncation? I'm not sure I follow — we saw latency improvements with quantized but maybe at cost of some context handling?

[01:25] Marco: Yeah, so on int8 path we observed some tokenization boundary differences and slightly different attention kernel ordering; in most cases it's fine but on long discharge notes the model sometimes omits medication lines leading to QA mismatches. it's subtle — transcription of medical entities isn't great in a couple examples.
[01:45] Priya: Hmm that fits what we saw in the dashboard — several fails were medication omission. Are those in the failure spreadsheet?
[01:50] Avery: They are in the shared sheet under 'discharge-summary-fails' with a sample of 120 fails. Marco, did you attach example prompts?
[01:56] Marco: yep, link in notes. quick caveat — some of the names got transcribed weirdly in the ETL, so you'll see 'Simons' vs 'Simmons' occasionally. auto-transcription noise.

[02:15] Sara Kim (Nexigen): on the prompt engineering side, v3 added an explicit "extract meds" step in the instruction. do you think that instruction could be causing the model to overfit to that phrasing and miss variants?
[02:25] Marco: Possible. We saw some anchor effects — the model latched onto the phrase and ignored inline meds when the note used shorthand. will test a paraphrase-ensemble approach.
[02:35] Jordan Li (Nexigen): also FYI our ingestion pipeline sometimes collapses abbreviations — e.g., 'ASA' -> 'aspirin' in some rows but not others. that's contributing to mismatch too.
[02:45] Avery: Good catch. sounds like two vectors: model/quantization edge-case + data normalization. action items split across us and you on that.
[02:52] Tom: On guardrails — can we add a post-filter to check for missing MEDICATIONS field and fallback to hosted model if not confident?

[02:59] Marco: Yes, Redwood supports fallback routing. we can add a confidence threshold and route those failing to a higher-accuracy variant or different quantization. that's a config change — low risk.
[03:12] Priya: What's the latency delta if we fallback to the higher-accuracy variant? we have 300 ms P99 SLO for this workflow.

[03:20] Marco: The higher-accuracy hosted variant clocks P95 ~420ms in our benchmark but P99 can spike to 700ms depending on token length. we can do partial responses: attempt fast path, if confidence low then run a targeted extra pass for only the medications segment to reduce compute and latency impact.

[03:40] Avery: Okay, tradeoff noted. For the regression investigation we'll (1) run targeted eval isolating long notes, (2) compare quantized vs fp16 on that slice, (3) test paraphrase ensemble for prompt wording.
[03:55] Marco: I'll schedule the expanded run — estimate 50k samples across slices, should finish in 2 days on dedicated pilot pool.
[04:05] Priya: Can you also surface the per-prompt tokenization diffs? that would help our ETL team.
[04:10] Marco: Yes, will include tokenization diff column in the spreadsheet.
[04:15] Sara: On safety/guardrails — can we get a breakdown of hallucination types? not just pass/fail but categories (meds missing, hallucinated lab values, wrong dates).
[04:23] Avery: Good ask. Marco, can the evaluator produce that breakdown?
[04:27] Marco: Yep, we have heuristic detectors for entity hallucination vs omission. will add categorical counts to the report.
[04:35] Jordan: procurement requested SOC2 and KMS details last week. any updates?

[04:40] Avery: I uploaded the security pack to the notes link. it includes SOC2 summary, KMS integration options, and recommended log retention settings. if you need the full attestation we can loop in security for formal sharing.
[04:52] Tom: We'll need the attestation for procurement — can you push that?
[04:55] Avery: Yes, I'll get the attestation out — timeline ~3 business days pending legal.
[05:00] Priya: For scoring, can you remind us of the metrics? we want to align on which metric triggers regression alerts.

[05:05] Marco: Primary metrics: QA exact-match rate, entity F1 (for meds), and human-eval severity score for hallucinations. alerts we recommend: drop in QA exact-match >5% week-over-week OR entity F1 drop >6% OR any increase in high-severity hallucinations.
[05:20] Priya: 5% seems fair. Can you attach the thresholds to the dashboard so we get email/Slack alerts?
[05:24] Marco: Yup, we can set alert rules; will need the Slack channel and threshold confirmation.
[05:30] Avery: Priya, Tom — what are your priorities for next week?
[05:34] Priya: fix the med omission regression first, then reduce hallucination on dates. After that, test guardrail fallback for low-confidence cases.
[05:42] Tom: Agree. also want network contact so we can test private deployment if fallback latency hits SLO breach.

[05:48] Avery: noted. summary of action items: Marco runs expanded eval + quantized vs fp16 slice; Avery shares scoring sheet + security attestation; Priya provides 200 additional edge-case prompts; Tom shares network contact. we'll reconvene next week same time; if we hit regressions earlier we'll spin up an ad-hoc deep dive.
[05:59] Marco: one more tiny note — we saw a small cost delta on the quantized runs but that's expected; Optimize team will share tuning knobs later if you want to reduce unit cost further.
[06:10] Priya: okay thanks, that's helpful. any final questions?
[06:14] Sara: none from product, good session.
[06:16] Avery: thanks all — I'll follow up with meeting notes and the security pack link. chat in slack if anything urgent. bye.
[06:20] (meeting ends)
